info.title: Hydrafetch API
info.description:
Hydrafetch is a web data API for developers and agents. Send a URL and get back clean Markdown, the page's own structured data, schema-shaped JSON, links, or a summary, with the navigation, banners and boilerplate stripped out. Scrape one page, crawl a whole site, run a search, or extract to a schema, all through one API with one response shape. Every call costs one credit a page whatever it took to fetch, and failures are never billed.

Point us at a whole site and get every page. Ask a question and get answers with per-field
confidence and the passage each value came from. You describe the outcome you want — the
pipeline decides how to get it.

## Authentication

Every request is authenticated with your API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Keys are scoped to a
workspace and carry its credit balance.

## Credits

Calls are billed in credits and charged only on success. A standard scrape is one credit; richer
formats and the extraction tier cost more. Each response reports what it consumed.

## Conventions

All timestamps are UTC ISO 8601. Long-running jobs (crawl, batch) return a job id you poll, or a
webhook you register.

## Errors

Every failure returns the same shape, whatever the status:

```json
{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS", "message": "Insufficient credits" },
  "meta": { "requestId": "019e8a3c-9f0b-7c12-88ab-1d2e3f4a5b6c" } }
```

Branch on `error.code`, which is stable. `error.message` is written for a person and may be
reworded without notice. Validation failures add `error.details`. Quote `meta.requestId` when
asking us about a specific failure. Every operation documents the codes it can return.

## Rate limits

Limits are per workspace, not per key, over a 60 second window, and the ceiling comes from your
plan. Every response carries the IETF RateLimit header fields so you can self-throttle rather
than discovering the limit by hitting it:

```http
RateLimit-Policy: "workspace";q=600;w=60
RateLimit: "workspace";r=599;t=42
```

`q` is the quota, `w` the window in seconds, `r` the requests remaining and `t` the seconds until
the window resets. A 429 also carries `Retry-After` in seconds; wait that long rather than
retrying immediately. The older `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and
`X-RateLimit-Reset` headers are still sent and mean the same thing.

## Versioning and deprecation

The version is in the path: every endpoint on this API lives under `/v1/`. Within a version we
only make additive changes — new endpoints, new optional parameters, new fields in a response.
Adding a field to a response is not a breaking change, so parse defensively and ignore what you
do not recognise.

Anything that would break an existing integration ships under a new version path instead. When an
endpoint or a version is retired, the responses say so before it stops working:

```http
Deprecation: @1780272000
Sunset: Sat, 01 May 2027 00:00:00 GMT
Link: <https://docs.hydrafetch.com/changelog>; rel="deprecation"
```

`Deprecation` (RFC 9745) marks when the endpoint became deprecated, `Sunset` (RFC 8594) when it
stops responding, and the `deprecation` link relation points at what to move to. Nothing on this
API is deprecated today, so you will not see these headers yet. Watch for them rather than for an
announcement: the headers are the notice, and the linked changelog carries what to move to.

post.description: Fetch a single URL and return it in the formats you ask for. Waits for the result by default, returning a job id if it runs long; set `async` to always return a job id immediately.

201.description: The scrape is running; poll the job id.

400.description: The request body or query failed validation.

402.description: The workspace has no credits left for this request. Nothing was charged and nothing was fetched.

error.message: Insufficient credits

403.description: The key is valid but the workspace may not make this request.

error.message: This workspace has been suspended and cannot make API requests.

404.description: No such job, or the id belongs to another workspace.

error.message: Job not found

422.description: The target site did not respond, so there was nothing to return. This is a fact about that URL rather than a fault on our side, and retrying it will not change the answer. Nothing was charged.

error.message: The origin did not respond to any attempt we made.

429.description: The workspace exceeded its per-minute request limit. Read the RateLimit headers, or Retry-After on this response, and retry after the window resets.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Prefer this over a fixed backoff.

RateLimit.description: Requests remaining (r) and seconds until the window resets (t).

RateLimit-Policy.description: The quota (q) for your plan and the window it applies over (w), in seconds.

schema.description: JSON Schema describing the shape you want the `json` format to return.

url.description: The URL to scrape. Must be http(s); a bare domain such as example.com is read over https.

maxAge.description: Serve from cache if a capture of this URL is younger than this many milliseconds. Omit for the default 24h window; 0 always fetches fresh. Capped at 7 days.

cacheOnly.description: Only serve from cache. If there is no fresh cached copy, return 404 instead of fetching.

storeInCache.description: Persist the capture for later re-extraction. Default true.

preferStructure.description: Preserve document structure (headings, lists, tables) over prose density — good for marketing and service pages. Default off.

async.description: Return a job id immediately instead of waiting for the result. Poll GET /v1/web/scrape/{id}. Opt in only: a synchronous call never degrades to a job id on its own, so you get a page or an error, not two response shapes.

onlyMainContent.description: Return only the main content, dropping nav/boilerplate. Default true.

includeTags.description: CSS selectors to keep. When set, only matching elements are considered.

excludeTags.description: CSS selectors to strip before extraction.

removeBase64Images.description: Strip inline base64 images from the output. Default true.

blockAds.description: Remove common ad and tracking elements. Default true.

includeLinks.description: Keep inline links in the markdown. Default true — a bare `Read the guide` is worth less to a model than one it can follow. Turn off for the densest possible prose.

waitFor.description: Extra milliseconds to let the page settle before capture.

timeout.description: Overall time budget for the request, in milliseconds.

headers.description: Extra request headers to send when fetching the page.

method.description: HTTP method to fetch the URL with. Use POST for endpoints that only answer a POST, such as JSON and GraphQL APIs. Defaults to GET.

body.description: Request body, sent verbatim. Only used when `method` is POST. Set the content type yourself via `headers`; nothing is assumed about the format.

formats.description: What to return. Omit for Markdown only. `structured` is the page's own data (no LLM, cheapest); `summary` and `json` are LLM-backed and cost more.

jsonOptions.description: Schema and/or prompt for the `json` format. One is required when `json` is requested.

structure.description: Whether the content carries markdown structure (headings, lists, emphasis) or is plain prose. `plain` is not an error — the default extractor optimises for capturing every word and wins on listing and forum pages. If you need the structure, re-request with `preferStructure: true`.

pageType.description: Coarse page classification (e.g. article, listing, forum, docs).

wordCount.description: Word count of the extracted main content.

description.example: A short summary of the page, as published by the page itself.
description.description: The page's own description (meta description / og:description).

publishedTime.description: When the page says it was published (ISO 8601).

modifiedTime.description: When the page says it was last updated (ISO 8601).

creditsUsed.description: Credits this call consumed. Charged only on success.

creditsRemaining.description: Credits left in your workspace's balance after this call.

freshness.description: Whether the result was served from cache or freshly fetched.

confidence.description: How trustworthy the extraction is, from 0 to 1. High when independent checks corroborate substantial content; near zero when the page yielded almost nothing.

complete.description: Whether the result captured the bulk of the content available on the page. False when the result looks thin or truncated.

blocked.description: Whether the page appeared to be behind a challenge or bot wall.

internal.description: Links pointing to the same site.

type.description: The schema.org type of the entity.

source.description: Which structured-data syntax the entity came from.

entities.description: The page's own structured data, normalised into one deduplicated list of typed entities.

jsonLd.description: Raw JSON-LD blocks, as found on the page.

appState.description: Names of embedded framework app-state blocks detected on the page.

finalUrl.description: The final URL after any redirects.

redirected.description: Whether the origin redirected: true when `finalUrl` differs from the URL you requested. Explicit so a page with no redirect is distinguishable from one whose redirect was not tracked.

status.description: HTTP status of the fetched page.

cached.description: Whether this result was served from cache.

warning.description: Set when the page was returned with a caveat (e.g. partial content).

markdown.description: Clean Markdown of the main content. Returned when `markdown` is requested.

html.description: Cleaned main-content HTML. Returned when `html` is requested.

rawHtml.description: The unmodified page HTML. Returned when `rawHtml` is requested.

summary.description: A concise factual summary. Returned when `summary` is requested (LLM-backed).

json.description: Schema-shaped JSON. Returned when `json` is requested (LLM-backed).

sitemapInclude.description: On sitemap-index sites, only descend into sub-sitemaps whose URL contains one of these comma-separated terms (case-insensitive). E.g. "post" to target article sitemaps.

sitemapExclude.description: Skip sub-sitemaps whose URL contains any of these comma-separated terms (case-insensitive). Compose with sitemapInclude — e.g. include "post" + exclude "tag,category,author" avoids WordPress taxonomy sitemaps (post_tag-sitemap, …-taxonomies-post_tag-*) that also contain "post".

order.description: Sort order by sitemap lastmod. "newest" (default) returns the most recent URLs first — the wanted end of a large archive under the limit. URLs without a lastmod sort last.

before.description: Cursor for paging a large archive newest→oldest: return only URLs with lastmod at or before this ISO timestamp. Page by passing the oldest lastmod from the previous page; dedupe by url across pages.

offset.description: Skip the first N results (in the sorted order) then return the next `limit`. Pagination for sources with no lastmod (WordPress-core), where the date cursor can't apply. Page sequentially (0, limit, 2·limit, …) so the sub-sitemap cache keeps deep pages fast.

includeSubdomains.description: Also include URLs on subdomains of the site. Default off.

ignoreQueryParameters.description: Treat URLs that differ only by query string as one. Default off.

lastmod.description: The <lastmod> from the sitemap, if present. null for links found on the page.

links.description: The site's discovered URLs, each with its sitemap lastmod (null when unknown).

total.description: Total URLs in the enumeration this page is a slice of. Page with `offset` until offset+count reaches this — do not infer the end from a short page.

truncated.description: Whether enumeration hit its ceiling or time budget. When true, `total` is a floor rather than the real size of the site.

url.description: The URL to POST events to. Must be a public http(s) URL — private, loopback, and link-local addresses are rejected.

events.description: Which events to receive. `page` fires as each page finishes; `completed` fires once when the job ends. Defaults to both.

headers.description: Extra headers to send with each callback, e.g. for authentication.

secret.description: A shared secret. When set, each callback carries an X-Hydrafetch-Signature header you can verify to prove the request came from us and is not a replay.

requestedUrl.description: For a batch, the URL exactly as you sent it, present only when it differed from `url` after normalisation (a trailing slash or #fragment). depth.description: How many links deep this page was from the start.

discoveredVia.description: How this URL entered the job. `requested` is a URL you gave us, meaning the crawl seed or a batch entry. `sitemap` came from the site's sitemap, `link` from following a link on a page we had already fetched.

error.description: Human-readable failure message. Set when this page failed.

errorCode.description: Stable machine-readable failure code. Set when this page failed.

retryable.description: When failed: true if it gave up after real retries (transient — safe to re-submit), false if a terminal failure.

kind.description: Which kind of job this is.

seedUrl.description: The starting URL, for a crawl.

creditsUsed.description: Credits consumed so far. One per scraped page.

status.description: pending while retries remain, success once delivered, failed once given up.

attempts.description: How many delivery attempts have been made.

responseStatus.description: HTTP status your endpoint returned on the last attempt.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, if it did.

createdAt.description: When the delivery was first created (ISO 8601).

source.description: `declared` the site said it in its own markup. `harvested` we processed an asset or read its CSS. `inferred` a model produced it from the page. `external` an enrichment source rather than the site.

level.description: How specific the answer is. `industry_group` is the 4-digit level, `national_industry` the 6-digit one.

confidence.description: How much evidence the classification found, not a model's self-report.

aspectRatio.description: Width over height — what a caller reserves layout space with.

name.description: Nearest CSS colour name, so a swatch reads as something and not only as six digits.

weight.description: How much the site itself uses it — the ranking that makes this the brand's colour.

kind.description: What kind of mark this is.

variant.description: Which background the asset is legible on. `mono` is a single-colour mark that works on both.

url.description: Public and immutable, so it can be embedded anywhere.

colors.description: The colours in the asset itself. A logo's own palette is the brand's, by definition.

blurhash.description: Tiny placeholder hash, so a client can render something before the image lands.

weight.description: How much of the site's type this face sets, 1 for the most-used one.

role.description: Absent when the page does not say which the face is.

domain.description: The canonical domain for this company.

queriedDomain.description: Only when you asked for a different domain that resolved here.

aliases.description: Only when this brand is known by more than its canonical domain.

description.example: Stripe powers online and in-person payment processing and financial solutions for businesses of all sizes.

tagline.example: Financial infrastructure to grow your revenue.

naics.description: Industry, as a real NAICS code rather than a phrase nobody can group on.

sources.description: Per-field provenance, keyed by field name. Lets you tell "their markup says this" from "a model guessed this".

data.description: Null when the domain could not be resolved at all. Unresolved domains are free.

url.description: Public and immutable, so it can be embedded anywhere.

data.description: Null when we hold no mark for the domain. A domain with no logo is free.

logo.description: The primary logo, so a picker can render a recognisable row.

data.description: One entry per requested domain, in the order you sent them. Null where unresolved.

files.description: Weight to file URL on the site's own servers, for a family that has no public source. The files are licensed to the site, so check the licence before linking to them. Empty for a Google family: use `stylesheet` instead.

stylesheet.description: For a family published on Google Fonts, its Google stylesheet, even when the site hosts its own copy.

role.description: Roles rather than a ranked list, so a colour drops straight into a theme instead of leaving you to guess which one is safe behind text.

textOnBackground.description: Contrast ratio of text against background.

meetsAA.description: Whether that ratio clears WCAG AA.

color.description: A hex color, or rgba() when the border is translucent.

kind.description: A layer the site draws behind or beside its panels: a patterned image, a solid block or an outline, offset to read as a shadow.

image.description: The pattern's image on the site's own server. Recreate it rather than linking to it.

count.description: How many boxes on the page share this treatment.

css.description: The panel as CSS declarations. A patterned decoration is not included; read `decoration` for it.

sticky.description: Whether the bar stays pinned while the page scrolls.

css.example: background-color: #0f172a; color: #ffffff; height: 72px; position: sticky; top: 0;

borderBottom.description: Absent with `border` set means the tab is open at the bottom, joined to the panel below.

css.example: background-color: #f9fafc; color: #0f172a; border: 2px solid #0f172a; border-bottom: none;

inactive.description: A tab that is not selected.

panel.description: The treatment most large boxes on the page share: cards, panels, framed sections.

headingOnPanel.description: Where a panel's title sits: across its top border like a fieldset legend, inside its padding, or just above it.

tabs.description: How the selected and other tabs are drawn.

band.description: A full-width section painted in a color far from the page, such as a dark hero band.

fallbacks.description: The rest of the declared stack, for rendering before the webfont arrives.

background.description: The fill. Absent on an outlined button, which has only a border.

minWidth.description: Width of the sampled button as it rendered, not a minimum the site sets. A button centring its label with flex has no padding to report, so this is the size to copy.

minHeight.description: Height of the sampled button as it rendered, not a minimum the site sets.

css.example: background-color: #533afd; color: #ffffff; border-radius: 4px; padding: 15.5px 24px; font-size: 16px; min-height: 48px;
css.description: The same button as CSS declarations you can paste into a rule.

page.description: The page that was read, when you asked for one with `url`.

mode.description: Whether the page as first loaded is light or dark. `colors` describe this mode.

dark.description: The colors the site switches to when the visitor prefers a dark theme. Null means we checked and the site does not change, so do not invent a dark palette from it. Absent on guides read before we checked.

components.description: How the parts are drawn, beyond the tokens: panel borders and decorative shadows, the header bar, and where headings sit on panels. This is what makes a site recognisable.

spacing.description: Keyed by step, for example `xs` through `xl`.

secondaryButton.description: The second call to action, painted differently from the first, or outlined.

contrast.description: Whether you can put text on what we handed you.

css.description: The same design as a stylesheet you can paste in: `@font-face` rules for the webfonts and a `:root` block of CSS variables for colors, fonts, the type scale, radius, shadows and spacing. Values that are not plain colors, lengths, font names or https font files are left out.

tailwind.description: The same tokens as a Tailwind CSS v4 stylesheet. Paste it as your main CSS file and classes such as `bg-accent`, `font-heading`, `text-h1`, `rounded-button` and `shadow-md` use the site's design.

shadcn.description: The colors, radius and fonts under shadcn/ui variable names (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--card`, `--muted`, `--border` and the rest). Replace the `:root` block in a shadcn project's globals.css with it.

data.description: Null when the domain could not be rendered. An unresolved domain is free.

url.description: The URL to harvest images from. Must be http(s).

maxAge.description: Serve from cache if a capture of this URL is younger than this many milliseconds. Omit for the default window; 0 always fetches fresh. Capped at 7 days.

src.description: The image URL, resolved to absolute.

alt.description: The image alt text, if any.

width.description: The image width in pixels, if declared.

height.description: The image height in pixels, if declared.

finalUrl.description: The final URL after any redirects.

images.description: Every image found on the page, with its metadata.

url.description: The URL to screenshot. Must be http(s).

fullPage.description: Capture the entire scrollable page instead of just the viewport. Default off.

waitFor.description: Extra milliseconds to let the page settle before capture.

timeout.description: Overall time budget for the request, in milliseconds.

maxAge.description: Reuse a stored screenshot if it is younger than this many milliseconds. Defaults to 7 days, so a repeated request returns the stored PNG with `cached: true` without re-rendering — which also means it returns immediately and does not apply `waitFor`. Pass 0 to force a fresh capture.

viewport.description: Screen size to render at. Defaults to desktop (1920x1080). Ignored when width/height are given explicitly.

viewportWidth.description: Exact viewport width in pixels. Overrides `viewport`.

viewportHeight.description: Exact viewport height in pixels. Overrides `viewport`. With fullPage the capture still extends to the full page height.

finalUrl.description: The final URL after any redirects.

status.description: HTTP status of the captured page.

screenshot.description: Public URL of the captured PNG. Stable for the same URL and options.

screenshotType.description: Whether the capture covers the whole scrollable page or just the viewport.

cached.description: True when a stored screenshot was reused instead of capturing a new one.

query.description: What to search the web for.

limit.description: How many ranked results to return. Omit for the default.

scrapeResults.description: When true, each result also comes back with its page fetched and returned as clean data, at 1 additional credit per page scraped. Defaults to false, which returns just the ranked title, url and snippet for the flat search credit.

timeRange.description: Restrict results to a recency window relative to now.

country.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code to bias results toward a region.

includeDomains.description: Only return results from these domains.

snippet.example: A rundown of the leading open source vector databases and how they compare.
snippet.description: A short snippet describing the result.

rank.description: The result's position in the ranked list.

data.description: The scraped page for this result, or null when scraping is off or unavailable.

status.description: Whether the search found anything: `ok` when it returned results, `no_results` when the web had no match. An empty `results` with `no_results` is a real miss — if the search cannot be completed at all, the request fails with 503 rather than returning an empty list.

urls.description: The pages to extract from. Each must be an http(s) URL. A trailing `/*` marks a crawl scope: every page discovered under that path is extracted and merged into the result.

schema.description: JSON Schema describing the shape you want back. Optional if `prompt` is given; when both are present the schema fixes the field names and types while the prompt guides what to pull.

prompt.example: Pull the product name, price in USD, and whether it is in stock.
prompt.description: Natural-language instruction for what to extract. Use with or instead of a schema.

preferStructure.description: Preserve document structure (headings, lists, tables) over prose density when reading the page — good for listing and catalog pages. Default off.

enableWebSearch.description: Pull in extra source pages by web-searching your prompt, to fill fields your URLs do not cover. Requires a `prompt`.

showSources.description: Return the concrete list of URLs that were actually extracted, after any wildcard and web-search expansion. Default off.

showConfidence.description: For each field, return a confidence score and the exact source passage the value was drawn from. Default off.

mergeEntities.description: Merge the per-page results into one deduplicated collection — one row per entity, with its contributing source URLs — instead of a separate result per page. Default off.

maxAge.description: Reuse a recent capture of each page if it is younger than this many milliseconds. Omit or 0 to always fetch fresh. Capped at 7 days.

confidence.description: How certain the value is correct given the page, from 0 to 1.

evidence.description: The exact short passage the value was drawn from, or an empty string if none.

url.description: The page this result came from.

data.description: The extracted data, shaped by your schema and/or prompt. Null when nothing matched.

fields.description: Per-field confidence and source passage, keyed by field name. Present only when `showConfidence` is set.

error.description: Set when this page could not be extracted; null on success.

data.description: The unioned data for one entity, filled across every contributing page.

sources.description: Every source URL that contributed to this entity.
The concrete URLs actually extracted, after wildcard and web-search expansion. Present only when `showSources` is set.

collection.description: The deduplicated collection, one row per entity. Present only when `mergeEntities` is set.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable reason. Branch on this rather than on the message, which may be reworded.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Safe to show a user, not to parse.

details.description: Optional machine-readable context, present on validation failures.

requestId.description: Quote this when contacting support about a specific failure.

WebError.description: Every failure on this API returns this shape, whatever the status. Successful responses never carry it.

tags.name: Scrape
tags.description: Turn one URL into clean, LLM-ready content. Ask for Markdown, HTML, links, or the page’s own structured data, and poll a job id when a fetch runs long.

tags.name: Crawl & batch
tags.description: Whole sites rather than single pages. Map every URL, crawl with depth and path rules, batch a list you already have, and read the webhook deliveries for either.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Search the web and get the ranked results back already scraped, so an agent has content to cite rather than links to fetch.

tags.name: Extract
tags.description: Pull schema-shaped JSON out of one or many pages, with optional per-field confidence and the source passage behind each value.

tags.name: Brand
tags.description: Resolve a domain into the company ready to render: logos for light and dark, the palette ranked by how the site uses it, fonts, socials, and the design system behind them.

tags.name: Media
tags.description: Images and screenshots from a page, with source and alt text, or a rendered capture of the page as it appears.
